description: The bar chart presents a comparative analysis of GLUE performance across seven fine-tuning methods—Prefix, Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S₁-model, S₄-model, and S₅-model—applied to two sizes of RoBERTa models: “base” (depicted in blue) and “large” (in orange), with performance values plotted on a linear vertical axis ranging from 86 to 90, marked at two-unit intervals. For each method, two adjacent bars show the respective performance of the base and large models. The Prefix method yields a base model score just under 85 and a large model score near 86. The Adaptor method exhibits a sharp drop for the base model (below 84) but achieves 88 for the large model. LoRA shows strong performance, with the base model reaching approximately 87 and the large model exceeding 89. BitFit displays a very low base model score (just above 84) while the large model scores around 88. The S₁-model shows modest gains, with both base and large models scoring around 86 and 87, respectively. The S₄-model sees the base model dip slightly below 86, while the large model again reaches 88. The S₅-model performs best overall, with the base model at 87 and the large model achieving the highest score on the chart—exactly 90. The legend in the upper left clearly maps blue to “base” and orange to “large,” and the bars are grouped by method along the horizontal axis without any specific sorting order, allowing direct comparison within each method across model sizes.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the GLUE performance of different fine-tuning methods for RoBERTa models of varying sizes. The horizontal axis represents the fine-tuning methods categorized as Prefix, Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S₁-model, S₄-model, and S₅-model, while the vertical axis shows the GLUE Performance on a linear scale, ranging from 86 to 90 with tick intervals at every two-unit increment. Each category contains two bars indicating the RoBERTa size, labeled and colored as 'base' in blue and 'large' in orange. For the Prefix method, the base model's performance is slightly below 85, while the large model reaches approximately 86. The Adaptor method shows a significant decline in performance for the base model, which drops below 84, while the large model reaches 88. The LoRA method demonstrates a consistent improvement, with the base model reaching 87 and the large model surpassing 89. The S₁-model shows a slight increase in performance for both sizes, with the base model reaching 86 and the large model reaching 87. The S₄-model shows a notable drop in performance for the base model, which falls below 86, while the large model reaches 88. Finally, the S₅-model shows the base model reaching 87, with the large model achieving the highest performance at 90. The legend at the top-right provides clarity on the color coding, and the bars are grouped by method but are not sorted in a specific order.
